title: Low-VOC vs. Zero-VOC Paint: What's Safer for Your Home?
description: Low-VOC and zero-VOC paints release fewer fumes, which matters most for nurseries, bedrooms and people sensitive to odors. Here's what the labels mean, their limits, and how to choose.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: VOCs (volatile organic compounds) are the chemicals that give fresh paint its smell and evaporate into the air as it dries. Low-VOC and zero-VOC paints release far fewer of them. They're a smart choice for nurseries, bedrooms and anyone sensitive to odors, and most quality interior paints today are low-VOC. "Zero-VOC" doesn't mean zero emissions, though, and good ventilation still matters.

What the Labels Mean

  • Low-VOC paints are usually defined as having 50 grams per liter or less of VOCs. Older and conventional paints can be much higher.

  • Zero-VOC paints are usually defined as having 5 grams per liter or less.

  • Third-party certifications, such as GREENGUARD Gold, test what the paint actually releases into indoor air. They're often a better guide than the VOC number alone.

Limits Worth Knowing

  • Colorants can add VOCs. The tint added to make deep colors can raise the VOC content of a "zero-VOC" base. Many brands offer low- or zero-VOC colorants; ask for them.

  • Low odor isn't the same as low VOC. Some products mask odor without cutting emissions.

  • Primers and specialty coatings vary. Stain-blocking primers and some oil-based or alcohol-based products have higher VOCs. They're sometimes still the right tool, so ventilation matters most on those days.

When Low- or Zero-VOC Paint Matters Most

  • Nurseries and kids' rooms. See our nursery painting page for timing tips before a baby arrives.

  • Bedrooms you'll sleep in the same night

  • Homes with people who have asthma, allergies or chemical sensitivities

  • Homes with pets, especially birds

  • Rooms with limited airflow

How to Reduce Fumes Whatever Paint You Use

  • Open windows and run fans to move air out of the room

  • Keep HVAC running to circulate and filter air, and change the filter after a big project

  • Keep children and pets out of freshly painted rooms for a day or two when possible

  • Seal and store leftover paint properly. See our guide to saving leftover paint.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is zero-VOC paint completely non-toxic?

No paint is completely free of chemicals. Zero-VOC paint releases very little, which makes it one of the best options for indoor air.

How long do paint fumes last?

With low-VOC paint and good ventilation, most odor fades within a day or two, though paint keeps curing for a few weeks.

Does low-VOC paint perform as well?

Today's premium low-VOC paints cover and wear as well as conventional paint. The difference is mostly smell and indoor air quality.
